records.question: How long does Spotify hold on to my personal information?
records.text: Spotify holds your personal information for as long as necessary to provide the Spotify Service and for legitimate business purposes, such as maintaining service performance and resolving disputes [Spotify – 6. Data retention]. Some data is retained until you delete it or until your Spotify account is deleted, such as your username and profile information. Streaming history is kept for the life of the account to provide personalized recommendations [Spotify – 6. Data retention]. Certain data, like search queries, is deleted after 90 days [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

records.question: Will Spotify give my money back if I cancel partway through a subscription period?
records.text: Spotify does not provide refunds or credits for any partial subscription periods, except as expressly stated in these Terms [Spotify – Billing and cancellation].

records.question: Can I team up with other Spotify customers to sue the company as a group?
records.text: No, you cannot team up with other Spotify customers to sue the company as a group. The Terms of Service state that neither party may participate as a plaintiff, claimant, or class member in any class, collective, consolidated, private attorney general, or representative proceeding [Spotify – Governing law, jurisdiction, class action waiver, and jury trial waiver].
cited_labels: [Spotify – Governing law, jurisdiction, class action waiver, and jury trial waiver]

records.question: How old do you need to be to open a Netflix account?
records.text: You need to be at least 18 years of age to create a Netflix account [Netflix – 1. The Netflix Service].

records.question: Can somebody who doesn't live with me use my Netflix plan?
records.text: Yes, someone who doesn't live with you can use your Netflix plan if you purchased an Extra Member account, which is available in certain countries [Netflix – 1. The Netflix Service].

records.question: How long does Netflix hang on to my details?
records.text: Netflix retains your personal information for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes described, such as providing their service, administering their business, and complying with laws [Netflix – Retention of Personal Information]. The exact duration depends on factors like your relationship with Netflix, the nature of the information, legal obligations, and the need to defend or resolve legal claims.

records.question: How long does Lyft store records of my past trips and payments?
records.text: Lyft stores records of your past trips and payments for at least seven years to ensure they can perform legitimate business functions, such as accounting for tax obligations [Lyft – How We Store and Protect Your Information].
cited_labels: [Lyft – How We Store and Protect Your Information]

records.question: Will Lyft charge me if I book a ride and never turn up?
records.text: Yes, Lyft may charge you if you book a ride and never turn up. If you fail to show up after requesting a ride, Lyft may charge a fee [Lyft – Charges].

records.question: Can a 17 year old ride with Lyft?
records.text: Yes, a 17-year-old can ride with Lyft under specific conditions. If the minor is using Rideshare Services, the parent or legal guardian must create a User account for the minor and ensure the use complies with safety instructions and applicable laws [Lyft – Eligibility]. Additionally, the minor must be accompanied by an adult if they are under 18 [Lyft – Driver Representations, Warranties and Agreements].

records.question: Is Lyft making money by selling my data?
records.text: Lyft does not sell your personal information to third parties for money [Lyft – How We Disclose Your Information]. However, they may share your personal information with third parties to deliver relevant personalized ads, which could involve "sharing" or the "sale" of personal information under certain local privacy laws [Lyft – How We Disclose Your Information]. Therefore, based on the provided information, Lyft is not explicitly making money by selling your data.

records.question: What's the youngest age allowed on Discord?
records.text: The youngest age allowed on Discord is 13 years old [Discord – Age requirements and responsibility of parents and legal guardians].
cited_labels: [Discord – Age requirements and responsibility of parents and legal guardians]

records.question: Does Discord sell what it knows about me to advertisers?
records.text: Discord may share information with advertising platforms to help reach people who might like their products and to measure the performance of their ads. This is done to bring more users to Discord and make their business successful, but they only provide the information needed for these services [Discord – How we disclose your information]. However, they do not make money from selling your personal information to third parties [Discord – A little bit about Discord].

records.question: What happens if a lot of people bring the same dispute against Discord at once?
records.text: If a lot of people bring the same dispute against Discord at once, the dispute may be resolved through arbitration, and the arbitration process may limit the ability to pursue claims as a class or representative action. Specifically, the Class Action Waiver provision states that any Dispute between you and Discord that is not subject to the "Agreement to Arbitrate" section may only be pursued on an individual basis, and you may not bring a claim as a plaintiff or class member in a class, collective, or representative action [Discord – Settling disputes between you and Discord]. Additionally, the Class Arbitration and Collective Relief Waiver provision states that, except as provided, you and Discord agree that each may bring claims against the other only in individual capacity, and not as a plaintiff or class member in any purported class or representative proceeding [Discord – Settling disputes between you and Discord].
cited_labels: [Discord – Settling disputes between you and Discord]

records.question: Are kids allowed to have a Reddit account?
records.text: Kids under the age of 13 are not allowed to create an account or otherwise use the Services [Reddit – Children].

records.question: What rights does Reddit get over the things I post?
records.text: Reddit gains the right to use your content worldwide, as you grant them a worldwide license to use that content when it is created with or submitted to the Services [Reddit – 5. Your Content]. You retain ownership rights, but you irrevocably waive any claims and assertions of moral rights or attribution with respect to your content [Reddit – 5. Your Content].

records.question: How long does Reddit hold on to my IP address?
records.text: Reddit holds your IP address for up to 100 days after collection. After that period, Reddit will delete any IP addresses collected [Reddit – What Information We Collect].

records.question: Will my paid Zoom plan keep billing me automatically?
records.text: Yes, your paid Zoom plan may keep billing you automatically. According to the Terms of Service, Zoom may charge your Payment Method for all Charges, including recurring fees, and unless otherwise specified, these Charges are subject to automatic renewals [Zoom – Effective Date: August 11, 2023]. Additionally, if you do not update your Payment Method promptly, Zoom may continue to charge your existing method [Zoom – 12. PAYMENTS AND CHARGES]. If you fail to pay Charges for five (5) calendar days following the due date, Zoom may terminate, suspend, or disconnect your Services [Zoom – 12. PAYMENTS AND CHARGES].

records.question: Can other people read my Zoom Email messages?
records.text: Yes, other people can read your Zoom Email messages under certain conditions. If the Zoom Email is not end-to-end encrypted, recipients can see, save, and share your email content [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?]. Additionally, account owners and designated account administrators can access email and calendar content sent to and from users on their Zoom Email or Zoom Calendar accounts, even if those emails are encrypted [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?]. Zoom also has access to email metadata used for basic email delivery, including email addresses in the from, to, cc, and bcc fields, time, mimeID, and the number and size of attachments [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?].
cited_labels: [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?]

records.question: Is Zoom allowed to shut down a service I'm paying for?
records.text: Yes, Zoom may shut down a service you're paying for under certain circumstances. For instance, if you fail to comply with any provision of the Agreement or any referenced policies, Zoom may suspend your access to the Services or terminate this Agreement [Zoom – 14. TERM; TERMINATION AND SUSPENSION]. Additionally, if there is a failure to pay Charges for five (5) calendar days following the due date, Zoom may terminate, suspend, or disconnect your Services immediately and without prior notice [Zoom – 12. PAYMENTS AND CHARGES]. Furthermore, Zoom may terminate this Agreement for any reason or no reason, upon thirty (30) business days’ advance notice [Zoom – 14. TERM; TERMINATION AND SUSPENSION].

records.question: Do I give up my right to a jury if I have a dispute with Coursera?
records.text: Yes, you give up your right to a jury if you have a dispute with Coursera. The Terms of Service include an arbitration agreement that waives your right to a jury trial [Coursera – Thank you for using Coursera!].

records.question: Could Coursera still have my data after I ask them to erase it?
records.text: Yes, Coursera may still have some of your data after you ask them to erase it. They may retain limited Personal Data where necessary for lawful and legitimate purposes, which may vary depending on your location, such as complying with legal obligations. records.question: Can a teenager sign up for their own PayPal account?
records.text: Yes, a teenager can sign up for their own PayPal account if they are at least 18 years old. If the teenager is under 18, they cannot open a personal account on their own and must have a parent or guardian open an account for them [Paypal – Opening an account].

records.question: How long does PayPal keep my information once I stop being a customer?
records.text: PayPal retains your Personal Information for as long as needed or is permitted in the context of the purpose for which it was collected and consistent with applicable law. Specifically, Personal Information used for the ongoing relationship between you and PayPal is stored for the duration of the relationship plus a period of 10 years or such period as mandated by any applicable local law once our relationship comes to an end, unless we need to keep it longer to the extent permitted by applicable law, such as when consistent with a legal obligation or for litigation, investigations, audit and compliance practices [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information].
cited_labels: [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information]

records.question: How much time do I have to get my money back from my bank for a PayPal SEPA debit?
records.text: You have up to 8 weeks to claim a refund from your bank for a PayPal SEPA Direct Debit payment [Paypal – Your continuous permission for us to charge your funding sources].

records.question: What age do I need to be to join Strava?
records.text: To join Strava, you need to be at least 13 years old. If you are under the legal age to form a binding contract in your jurisdiction, your parent or legal guardian must review and agree to these Terms on your behalf [Strava – Registration and Accounts].

records.question: Can I get my Strava subscription money back?
records.text: Strava's Terms of Service do not specifically mention a refund policy for subscription fees. However, if you signed up for a free trial, you may cancel your subscription before the end of the trial period to avoid being charged. If you cancel after the trial, your Payment Method will be authorized for up to approximately one month of service, but no charges will be made unless you do not cancel prior to the end of your free trial period [Strava – Free Trials]. For subscription fees paid in advance, refunds are not mentioned in the provided documents. Not found in the documents.

records.text: Not found in the documents

records.question: If I close my Strava account, does my data actually go away?
records.text: Yes, when you close your Strava account, your personal information is permanently and irreversibly deleted from their systems, including backups. However, it may take up to 45 days to fully delete your personal information and system logs from their systems [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data]. Additionally, Strava may retain some information to comply with the law, prevent fraud, collect fees, resolve disputes, troubleshoot problems, assist with investigations, enforce the Terms of Service, and take other actions permitted by law [Strava – Retention of Information].
cited_labels: [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data]

records.question: What can Pinterest do with the pictures I upload?
records.text: Pinterest can use the pictures you upload to show you content and ads on and off Pinterest that are relevant to you [Pinterest – 1. The Service]. You retain all rights in, and are solely responsible for, the User Content you post to Pinterest [Pinterest – a. Posting User Content]. If you upload pictures that infringe the intellectual property rights of others, Pinterest can take action against such content, including removing, restricting, or limiting access to it [Pinterest – a. Posting User Content].

records.question: Does Pinterest use the websites I visit to show me ads?
records.text: Yes, Pinterest uses the websites you visit to show you ads. They use information such as cookie IDs, your IP address, and a hashed version of your email address to disclose to services they use to market Pinterest to you on sites and apps other than Pinterest, such as Facebook Ads, Google Marketing Platform, and others [Pinterest – To deliver ads, off Pinterest, that are relevant, interesting and personal to you about Pinterest, we:]. Additionally, they may show you ads for other outdoor products if you show an interest in camping tents on Pinterest or browse sleeping bags on one of our partner’s websites [Pinterest – We also use your information to personalize the ads you see].
